versions.description: Full crossplatform support, Installer/Updater/File migrator available, Tui & Gui clients, Auto game playtime tracking
changelog: [Major change]: Refactored the entire app in C#, to be able to build more faster

[Major Change]: Fragmented how the 'app' works, into pieces, the automatic game monitor service, the client, setup, instead of the original full suite inside a single binary, which resulted in bad results sometimes (like closing the app while tracking games)

[Major new feature]: The 'client', they enable the user to interact with the settings and game library files. The client also has similar features similar to the the initial 1.1.0 app but now its not tied to tracking automatic games. Currently there is the TUI client (in the terminal/console), and the GUI client (unique and more beautiful window, though uses more resourses)

[Major new feature]: The 'Automatic game', you can move your games which now they are of type 'Manual game', or add new ones to be able now to have the ability to not even have to interact with the 'client' to start/stop a game, its all automatic, when you start your game or exit, the automatic game monitor service adds your elapsed time.

[Major new feature]: The 'Automatic game monitor service', a service which starts when your computer starts, and monitors whenever your added games (in the client) are active, tracking your in-game playtime. This way you don't even have to keep the client active, neither have to worry on anything. The service is very efficient and doesn't waste when working, and almost nothing when waiting for active games.

[Major new feature]: The 'Setup', an app used whenever you want to install new clients, update versions, or even migrate files manually between older or newer versions! And for power users, if you don't want to use the TUI interface, you can use the CLI interface by giving any argument to it and reading then the documentation given by the app.
[Change]: Moved from json file format for AppSettings and GameLibrary to a sqlite3 database format
[Fixed known issue]: In case of a power outage, when writing to AppSettings or GameLibrary, they could get corrupted but now as we have moved to a sqlite3 database, this issue is almost impossible
[Removed]: Ability to stop games from being automatically saved and also being able change the interval at which the app saves games. This is replaced with better defaults and better user experience
[Note]: Because the entire project moved to C# & because of it growth, memory consumption, cpu usage and disk requirements have increased, but acceptable & still very 'light' compared to other apps

[Note]: Manual games are still automatically saved each auto save interval, though its now forced enabled and the interval its forced to be 5 minutes. If wanted to have the ability to change this in the client, submit an issue on the GitHub page.

[Note]: You as the user don't need to much interact with the new service or the setup ussually. Its only when you need them, as 'GameWatch' manages it all, updating, monitoring. Though we still require the user to hit the update button in the client (which starts the updater in cli mode), or starting yourself the setup app
[Note]: The automatic game monitor service checks for new game status each 5 seconds, value forced, unchangable by the user

[Forced limitation]: GameWatch now uses the system default folder for its storage, instead of leaving it up to the user. This is made to give access for the service to start at computer startup, to make it easier to update/install newer versions
[Limitations]: The setup app cannot remove older version e.g: 1.0.1, 1.1.0, because it doesn't control the folders

versions.description: Linux support & Windows static runtime linking
changelog: [New]: Linux prebuilt binary available for download
[Fixed]: On windows the app doesn't required the user to have installed 'Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable', as it statically links
[Changed]: Changed internally the library provider from vcpkg to using cmake's fetch_content feature
[Changed]: On windows instead of forcing the user to use openssl, we use WinSSL
[Note]: The linux prebuilt binary was compiled on Windows 11 WSL2 Fedora. Take that into consideration if you have issues, meaning you might have to compile the app yourself.
[Known issue]: In case the user experiences a power outage, and the app is writing to any json file, the file might get corrupted :/
[Added]: Everything, new release from ground up
[Note]: This release provides prebuilt binaries only for Window, as it was coded in C++; This is fixed in release 1.1.0
[Note]: This release required users to have installed a certain 'Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable', though ussually installed on most computers; This is fixed in release 1.1.0
[Known issue]: In case the user experiences a power outage, and the app is writing to any json file, the file might get corrupted :/
